From: Eleanor Shaw <eleanor.shaw@acmef.com>

Date: 2027-02-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Event alert — short-lived snapshot leak?

Sergio,

We detected a short-lived telemetry snapshot in a staging bucket that appears to contain hashed customer identifiers related to one dataset we share with Redwood. Security flagged it as a "limited exposure" — no PII in plain text, but it's still in scope for our DPA clause on "personal data exposures."

Primary asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether any production traffic or backups were involved?
- We need an initial incident window and an indication of which subprocessors (if any) had access in the last 30 days.
- Please propose a cooperation timeline so our legal/compliance team can prepare the evidence request (we're aiming for a 72-hour initial response).

Eleanor Shaw
Head of Security Operations
Acme Financial

Subject: Re: Event alert — short-lived snapshot leak?

Eleanor — thanks for the heads-up. We take this seriously. Quick update from infra while we pull logs:

- Preliminary: no production GPUs or persistent backups show read activity to that bucket in the past 45 days. It looks like a short-lived staging snapshot created by a telemetry job.
- Subprocessors: CloudVendor (metrics ingestion) had transient access to the staging pipeline during the job run window.

Proposed cooperation timeline (subject to confirmation by 12:00 PT):
1) 0–6 hours: initial facts & scope (we'll confirm whether any user identifiers are reversible).
2) 6–48 hours: shared evidence package (audit trail, access logs, minimal dataset export under NDA).
3) 48–120 hours: deeper forensic handover if needed (forensic snapshot export, KMS audit).

We're attaching a draft redline for the DPA incident sections that clarifies short-lived exposures, subprocessors' transient access, and a concrete evidence handover cadence.

Action: Kimberly, Ben — please start the log pull (job ids, bucket ACLs) and flag anything that expands the window. Laura, please prep a redline with discrete timeline wording and a cooperation clause that limits data transfer to forensics only.

Sergio Alvarez
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-03-01T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Event alert — limited exposure — subprocessor & cross-border coordination

Eleanor — thanks for your patience. Per Sergio's team, here's the consolidated response and proposed contractual language.

Facts established (summary):
- Exposure type: staging telemetry snapshot (hashed identifiers; no clear PII).
- Scope: single staging bucket; retention policy removed object within 36 hours.
- Subprocessor access: CloudVendor ingestion role had transient read access during the job run. No production systems or backups were involved.

Proposed cooperation & DPA language (suggested redline excerpts):
1) Incident window: "The provider will acknowledge receipt of an incident alert within 6 hours and provide an initial scoping statement within 72 hours specifying systems, subprocessors, and a proposed evidence handover schedule."
2) Subprocessor clause: "Where a subprocessor may have had transient access to data relevant to an incident, the provider shall coordinate with that subprocessor and procure access logs and a limited, read-only forensic snapshot within 48 hours of the customer's written request; such snapshot shall be exported under mutually agreed encryption and transfer controls and may only be used for investigative purposes as defined in this DPA."
3) Data residency / cross-border: "If an investigative export requires cross-border transfer, the provider shall notify the customer and, where required by applicable law or the DPA, obtain prior written consent before transferring any data outside the EEA/US region; emergency exports required by law enforcement may be handled under the lawful access coordination procedure set forth in Section X."

Action items:
- Acme: confirm whether the 72-hour initial scoping window is acceptable.
- Redwood: Ben to attach the proposed redline (we're attaching a PDF and a redline summary).

Laura Bennett
VP, Privacy & Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-dpa-proposed-incident-clauses-redline.pdf]

Laura / Sergio — appreciate the quick triage and the clear redline language. A few clarifications from our compliance team:
- 72-hour initial scoping is acceptable. We need the initial scoping to include whether any reversible identifiers exist and an estimate of affected records (even if 0).
- On cross-border: Acme requires customer consent for any transfer outside the US. An emergency lawful-access carveout is fine but we'd like the notification requirement to be explicit (notify within 24 hours if an export crosses borders).

If Redwood can commit to the proposed subprocessor 48-hour access-log procurement and to notify Acme within 24 hours of any cross-border export, we will treat this as the cooperation plan and proceed with our internal containment steps.

Eleanor
